questions.stem: A batch job moves from Java 11 to Java 17 with its start script unchanged. The script passes `--illegal-access=permit`, and a caching library calls `setAccessible(true)` on the private `table` field of `java.util.HashMap` during startup. What happens?

options.text: The JVM warns that it ignores the option, and the call throws InaccessibleObjectException, since that package is not opened to the library
options.says: Java 17 removed --illegal-access; the JVM ignores it with a warning, and deep reflection on a non-opened JDK package throws InaccessibleObjectException

options.text: The JVM warns that it ignores the option, and the call throws SecurityException, since a refused reflective access counts as a security failure
options.says: the refusal is InaccessibleObjectException, an unchecked exception that is not a SecurityException, so a catch written for SecurityException misses it

options.text: The JVM accepts the option, and the call succeeds after one warning line, since the option opens the packages the JDK had before modules
options.says: that was the behaviour up to Java 16; Java 17 removed the option and ignores it

options.text: The JVM rejects the option, and the job never reaches the call, since an option the JVM no longer supports stops the launch
options.says: the JVM prints a warning that it ignores the option and starts; the failure comes later, at the reflective call

origin.section: Java 17 Refuses Deep Reflection into the JDK, and --illegal-access Is Gone

questions.stem: A team ships a Java 21 service as a `jlink` image built with the modules `jdeps --print-module-deps` reports for its jar: `java.base,java.sql`. At startup the service calls `RandomGeneratorFactory.of("Xoshiro256PlusPlus").create(seed)`. What happens?

options.text: The call returns a seeded generator, since the factory and the algorithms it creates are all part of java.base
options.says: on 21 the interface and factory are in java.base, but the LXM and Xoshiro algorithms are in jdk.random

options.text: The call returns a generator of the default algorithm, since the factory falls back when the named one is missing
options.says: an unavailable name throws IllegalArgumentException; nothing falls back

options.text: The call throws IllegalArgumentException, since the module holding that algorithm is not in the image
options.says: the algorithms live in jdk.random and are found through ServiceLoader, so jdeps doesn't list the module and the image lacks it

options.text: The jlink step fails, since jdeps reports the module holding that algorithm as a missing dependency
options.says: jdeps sees no reference to jdk.random, since the algorithms are found through ServiceLoader, so it doesn't list the module and the build succeeds; the failure comes at run time

origin.section: Spot the Problem: A Trimmed Runtime Has No Algorithms

questions.stem: A retry helper keeps `private static final ThreadLocalRandom JITTER = ThreadLocalRandom.current();`, initialised on the main thread. A pool of new worker threads calls `JITTER.nextLong(500)` for each retry delay and never calls `ThreadLocalRandom.current()` itself. The service is restarted on the same machine with the same JVM flags. What do the workers draw?

options.text: Each worker draws the same delays it drew before the restart, since those threads' generator state was never seeded
options.says: the stored instance reads the calling thread's state; a thread that never called current() has an unseeded state, so its numbers follow from its id and repeat across restarts

options.text: Each worker draws delays unrelated to the ones before the restart, since every thread's generator is seeded when it first draws
options.says: only current() seeds the calling thread; drawing through a stored instance doesn't

options.text: All workers draw from one generator owned by main, and some delays come out twice, since the instance carries main's state
options.says: the stored instance reads the state of whichever thread calls it, so the workers don't draw from main's state; each draws from its own

options.text: All workers draw one shared sequence in turn, with no repeats, since the instance is thread-safe like Random
options.says: the workers don't share one sequence; the page's run shows each thread drawing its own, unseeded here

origin.section: A Generator Shared Across Threads Is Either Slow or Wrong

questions.stem: A plugin host is built with `javac --release 11`. At startup it calls `System.setSecurityManager(new SecurityManager())` inside `try { ... } catch (RuntimeException e) { log.warn("no sandbox", e); }`. It moves from Java 17 to Java 21 with no new JVM options. What do the build and the Java 21 run show?

options.text: javac gives no removal warning, and on 21 the sandbox still installs, since a method deprecated for removal works until it is removed
options.says: since Java 18 setSecurityManager throws UnsupportedOperationException unless the JVM starts with -Djava.security.manager=allow

options.text: javac gives no removal warning, and on 21 the plugins run without a sandbox, since the call throws and the catch carries on
options.says: --release 11 compiles against the 11 API, so no removal warnings; on 21 the call throws UnsupportedOperationException, which the catch logs before startup continues

options.text: javac gives removal warnings, and on 21 the plugins run without a sandbox, since the call throws and the catch carries on
options.says: with --release 11 javac checks against the 11 API, where nothing here was deprecated, so it gives no removal warnings

options.text: javac gives removal warnings, and on 21 the sandbox still installs, since 21 installs it with a warning as 17 did
options.says: with --release 11 there are no removal warnings, and 21 refuses the install by default

origin.section: The Security Manager Still Compiles, Warns, and Since 18 Refuses to Install
